abfahren.kurz: Get in lane early, use the exit lane, only brake there

k0.text: The advance direction sign announces the exit 1000 m ahead. Plan now: move to the right-hand lane early – not at the last second from the left.

frage.text: When do I move to the right?
optionen: Early, at the latest before the countdown markers
Doesn't matter, across the hatched area if necessary
frage.erklaerung: Get in lane in good time so the lane change works without rushing or endangering anyone.

k1.text: Indicate right, check the interior and exterior mirrors, shoulder check to the right – then move briskly into the right-hand lane.

k2.text: Stay in the right-hand lane and keep your speed. Switch the indicator off again.

k3.text: The exit is announced once more 500 m ahead. From now on, avoid overtaking if possible.

k4.text: Markers with 3, 2, 1 stripes: 300, 200, 100 m left until the start of the exit lane.

frage.text: What does the marker with two stripes mean?

k5.text: Indicate right in good time before the exit lane – the traffic behind you must see it early.

k6.text: Mirrors and shoulder check to the right, then cross the wide broken line into the exit lane.

k7.text: Only reduce your speed once you are in the exit lane, not before on the motorway. There you must not drive faster than in the through lanes.

frage.text: Where do I reduce my speed?
frage.erklaerung: Braking on the motorway endangers the traffic behind you – only slow down in the exit lane, and reach the indicated speed before the bend.

k8.text: Brake down to the indicated speed limit (here 60 km/h) by the time you reach the sign, before the bend gets tighter. After a long motorway drive, 60 km/h feels very slow – check your speedometer!

frage.text: Why look at the speedometer?
optionen: Because after driving fast you misjudge your speed
frage.erklaerung: After a motorway drive you underestimate your own speed (you get used to it).

k9.text: Missed the exit? Drive on to the next one. Never reverse or turn around on the motorway – not even on the hard shoulder.

auffahren.kurz: Acceleration lane, find a gap, merge

k0.text: The slip road leads to the motorway in its own curve. Already watch the motorway traffic here: How fast is it, where are the gaps?

frage.text: Who will have right of way when merging in a moment?
optionen: Me – I'm in the acceleration lane
The traffic on the main carriageway
frage.erklaerung: § 18 Abs. 3 StVO: The traffic on the main carriageway has right of way.

k1.text: In the acceleration lane, briskly speed up to the speed of the traffic. Here you may drive faster than in the through lanes – that is intended.

frage.text: What is the most important task now?
optionen: Briskly accelerate to the speed of the traffic
frage.erklaerung: At a speed similar to the traffic you can merge safely. Merging too slowly forces others to brake.

k2.text: Announce the lane change in good time and clearly – indicate left.

frage.text: When do I indicate?
optionen: Only when I'm already changing lanes
frage.erklaerung: Every lane change must be announced in good time and clearly (§ 7 Abs. 5 StVO).

k3.text: The lorry is ahead on the right, the red car is keeping a large distance. The gap behind the lorry fits: match your speed and keep enough distance (rule of thumb: half the speedometer reading in metres).

frage.text: Where do I merge?
optionen: Into the gap behind the lorry
In front of the lorry, I'll step on it
frage.erklaerung: The gap behind the lorry is big enough. In front of it things would get tight, and it has right of way.

k4.text: Just before the change: interior and exterior mirrors, then a shoulder check to the left – otherwise the blind spot stays invisible.
k4.regel: § 7 Abs. 5 StVO: rule out any danger to others

frage.text: What comes directly before the lane change?
optionen: Mirrors and shoulder check to the left
frage.erklaerung: Only with a shoulder check can you see a vehicle in the blind spot.

k5.text: Cross over the wide broken line – not over the solid line or the hatched area. Move across briskly and smoothly, don't wait until the end of the lane.

k6.text: After the change, switch the indicator off and keep driving on the right. Distance to the lorry ahead: at least half the speedometer reading in metres.

frage.text: And now?
optionen: Overtake on the left straight away
Indicator off, drive on the right, keep your distance
frage.erklaerung: Keep-right rule (§ 2 Abs. 2 StVO) and sufficient distance (§ 4 Abs. 1 StVO).

k7.text: The zip merge (Reißverschlussverfahren) does not apply when joining the motorway: whoever joins must give way. If there is no gap, stop at the end of the lane if necessary – never swerve onto the hard shoulder.
k7.regel: § 18 Abs. 3 StVO · § 7 Abs. 4 does not apply here

doppel.kurz: Two turning lanes – everyone stays in their lane

k0.text: Both lanes lead to the left (arrows, Sign 297), the traffic light is green. Get in lane in good time, indicate – and stay in the lane you have chosen.

frage.text: The driving school car is in the right-hand of the two left-turn lanes. Which lane does it turn into?
optionen: Into the right-hand lane of the road it is turning into
frage.erklaerung: Left stays left, right stays right – that way there is no conflict with the car next to you.

k1.titel: Keep your lane through the turn
k1.text: Turn side by side, evenly. The broken guide lines in the junction show the way. No lane changes in the junction!

k2.text: Only after the junction – with indicator, mirrors and shoulder check – change lanes if needed.

ecke.titel: Reversing round a corner to the right
ecke.kurz: Reversing into a side road – evenly and close to the kerb

k0.text: Stop at the right-hand edge of the road about two to three car lengths past the side road. All-round check – other traffic has priority.

frage.text: What is most important when reversing?
optionen: Driving slowly and watching all around
Only looking in the interior mirror
frage.erklaerung: When reversing, nobody may be endangered – go slowly, looking back and all around.

k1.text: Turn your body, look through the rear window and roll straight back – about 50 cm from the kerb.

k2.text: When the rear wheel reaches the corner: steer to the right so that the car follows the curve of the kerb evenly. The front swings out to the left into the road – look all around again first!

frage.text: Which way do I steer so that the rear goes to the right?
frage.erklaerung: When reversing: turn the steering wheel in the direction you want the rear to go.

k3.text: Once the car is parallel to the kerb of the side road: straighten the steering wheel and reverse about one more car length.

eng.kurz: Whoever has to pass the obstacle lets oncoming traffic through

k0.text: A lorry is standing on my side with its hazard lights on. The road is too narrow for two vehicles side by side.

frage.text: Who may go through the narrowing first?
optionen: The oncoming traffic – the obstacle is on my side
frage.erklaerung: § 6 StVO: Anyone who wants to pass an obstacle on the left must let oncoming vehicles through.

k1.text: Stop in good time and at a distance from the obstacle – that leaves room to pull out and you can see oncoming traffic better.

k2.titel: Signal that you are pulling out
k2.text: When it's clear: mirrors, shoulder check to the left, indicate left and pass the lorry with enough side clearance – watch out for people getting out.

k3.text: After the obstacle, indicate right and move back to the right.

gefahr.kurz: Reaction distance + braking distance = stopping distance – with reaction test

k0.text: Two drives compared in the same lane: the driving school car at 50 km/h and – semi-transparent – the same car at 30 km/h. In a moment a ball will roll onto the road between the parked cars, and a child will run after it.

k1.text: About 1 second passes before your foot is on the brake. During this time the car keeps going without braking: almost 14 m at 50 km/h, just over 8 m at 30 km/h.

frage.text: How long is the reaction distance at 50 km/h (rule of thumb)?
frage.erklaerung: (50 ÷ 10) · 3 = 15 m. The exact calculation gives about 14 m per second.

k2.text: Press the brake and clutch fully at the same time and keep the pressure on. The ABS rattles – that is intended. Keep a relaxed grip on the steering wheel so you can swerve.

frage.text: How long is the braking distance in an emergency stop from 50 km/h (rule of thumb)?
frage.erklaerung: (50 ÷ 10)² ÷ 2 = 12.5 m. Normal braking distance (no emergency): (50 ÷ 10)² = 25 m.

k3.text: The 30 km/h car stops in time. At 50 km/h the distance isn't enough – at the spot where the ball is, the car would still be going about 35 km/h. 30 km/h saves lives.

frage.text: Why is a 30 km/h limit outside schools so important?
optionen: The stopping distance is much shorter – at 50, at the point where I would already have stopped at 30, I'm still going almost as fast as when I started braking
frage.erklaerung: The braking distance increases with the square of the speed.

gruenpfeil.kurz: Stop first, then turn right carefully – traffic with a green light goes first

k0.text: The traffic light shows red. Next to it on the right there is a green arrow on a black metal sign (Sign 720) – not a light arrow!

frage.text: What does the green arrow require first?
optionen: Stop completely at the stop line
frage.erklaerung: After stopping, turning right at red is permitted – stopping is mandatory.

k1.text: Stop completely. In front of me a pedestrian is crossing the road on green.

frage.text: Who goes first?
optionen: Pedestrians and cross traffic with a green light
frage.erklaerung: Any obstruction or danger – especially to pedestrians and vehicles with a green light in their direction – must be ruled out.

k2.titel: Edge forward to the sight line
k2.text: The crossing is clear. Edge forward slowly to the sight line and stop again.

k3.text: A car is coming from the left on green – it must be neither obstructed nor endangered. Wait.

k4.text: The blue car has passed. Shoulder check to the right and turn slowly – only from the right-hand lane!

k5.text: A lit green arrow in the traffic light = its own green phase for turning. Green metal sign = turn only after stopping, with the greatest care.

kreisel.kurz: Enter without indicating, traffic on the roundabout has right of way, indicate when leaving

k0.text: Roundabout with "Give way": traffic on the roundabout has right of way. Approach slowly and look to the left.

frage.text: Do I indicate when entering the roundabout?
optionen: No – indicating when entering is not allowed
frage.erklaerung: § 9a Abs. 1 StVO: Using the indicator when entering is not permitted.

k1.text: The blue car is already on the roundabout and has right of way. Stop at the give-way line and let it pass.

k2.text: Clear – enter without indicating. On the roundabout you drive anticlockwise; stopping on the roundabout is prohibited.

k3.text: After passing the exit before yours, indicate right, mirrors and shoulder check to the right – cyclists and pedestrians!

frage.text: When do I indicate to exit?
optionen: After the exit before mine – in good time before leaving
frage.erklaerung: Leaving is announced: indicate right as soon as you have passed the exit before your own.

k4.text: After the exit there is a zebra crossing. Anyone who wants to use it has priority – approach at moderate speed and wait.

frage.text: The pedestrian wants to use the zebra crossing. Who has priority?
optionen: Me – I'm coming out of the roundabout
frage.erklaerung: § 26 Abs. 1 StVO: Pedestrians who clearly want to use the crossing must be allowed to cross.

laengs.kurz: Sideways into a parking space at the edge of the road

k0.text: Does the space fit? Rule of thumb: at least one good car length plus about 1.5 m. Indicate right early so the traffic behind knows what you are doing.

frage.text: When do I indicate?
optionen: Not at all, I'm only parking
frage.erklaerung: Indicate right early – that way the traffic behind you understands why you are stopping.

k1.titel: Stop next to the car in front
k1.text: Stop parallel next to the front car, about 50 cm to 1 m to the side. Your rear is roughly level with its rear.

frage.text: What comes before reversing?
optionen: All-round check – especially to the rear
frage.erklaerung: Look all around before every movement; when reversing, turn your body and look through the rear window.

k2.text: Roll back slowly while steering fully to the right. The rear swings into the space. Keep looking back; the front swings out to the left into the road – look again first!

k3.text: Straighten the steering wheel and roll straight back a little – this brings the car closer to the kerb.

k4.text: When the right front corner has passed the rear of the car in front: steer fully to the left. The car turns parallel to the kerb.

frage.text: When do I steer to the left?
optionen: When the front has passed the car in front
frage.erklaerung: Steering back too early makes the front hit the other car – too late puts the rear against the kerb.

k5.text: Move forward a little until there is roughly the same space in front and behind. Goal: parallel and close to the kerb (guide value: up to about 30 cm), without touching it.

frage.text: How far from the kerb may the car be?
optionen: Close – guide value up to about 30 cm
frage.erklaerung: Well parked: parallel and close to the kerb – but without touching it.

links_gegen.kurz: Oncoming traffic and oncoming right-turners have priority

k0.text: Mirrors, indicate left, move towards the centre. Before moving over, watch the traffic behind you.

frage.text: Where do I position myself to turn left?
optionen: Up to the centre of the road
On the opposite side of the road
frage.erklaerung: Turning left: position up to the centre (in one-way streets as far left as possible).

k1.text: Drive forward into the junction and wait. Keep the wheels straight – if you are hit from behind, you won't roll into oncoming traffic.

frage.text: In which order may the vehicles go?
frage.erklaerung: Anyone turning left lets oncoming traffic through – including the right-turner from opposite. The driving school car goes last.

k2.text: Vehicles going straight on and right-turners from opposite have priority. Only turn when everything is clear and no pedestrians are crossing any more.

k3.text: In the road I'm turning into, a pedestrian is crossing. Take special care – wait until he is across.

frage.text: The pedestrian is still in the road. What do I do?
frage.erklaerung: When turning, take special care of pedestrians – wait if necessary.

k4.text: Immediately before turning: shoulder check to the left (cyclists, overtaking vehicles), then turn briskly in a wide arc.

quer_rueck.kurz: Reversing into a parking bay – later drive out forwards with a good view

k0.text: Drive slowly along the aisle, indicate right and drive past the space until your rear is about 1–2 m beyond it.

k1.text: Look all around before reversing – pedestrians and cars in the aisle!

frage.text: Why reverse into the bay?
optionen: You have a good view ahead when driving out later
frage.erklaerung: Going in backwards lets you steer more tightly, and when leaving you can see the cross traffic.

k2.text: Reverse slowly and steer fully to the right. Look back and at the corners of the neighbouring cars.

k3.text: When the car is parallel to its neighbours: straighten the steering wheel and roll back centrally to the end of the space.

frage.text: When do I straighten the steering?
optionen: As soon as I'm in the space
When the car is parallel to the neighbouring cars
frage.erklaerung: Then continue straight – otherwise the car ends up at an angle.

quer_vor.kurz: Forwards into a parking bay – swinging out first

k0.text: Drive slowly along the aisle towards the space, indicate right. Swing out a little to the left so the arc fits into the space.

frage.text: Why do I swing out before parking forwards?
optionen: So the arc fits into the narrow space
frage.erklaerung: When driving forwards, the rear wheels cut the corner on the inside – swinging out prevents the rear from scraping the neighbouring car.

k1.text: When the middle of the space is roughly level with the exterior mirror: steer fully to the right. Watch the corners of the neighbouring cars (shoulder check to the right).

k2.text: Straighten the steering wheel and roll centrally into the space until the front is just short of the end. It must be possible to get out on both sides.

frage.text: What is the disadvantage when leaving the space later?
optionen: Reversing out – poor view of the traffic
frage.erklaerung: That's why reverse parking is recommended: you then drive out forwards with a good view.

rechts_rad.titel: Turning right with a cycle path
rechts_rad.kurz: Shoulder check – the cyclist going straight on has priority

k0.titel: Move to the right and indicate
k0.text: Mirrors, indicate right, position as far right as possible. There is a cycle path to the right of the road.

frage.text: Who has priority here?
frage.erklaerung: § 9 Abs. 3 StVO: Anyone turning must let cyclists through who are travelling in the same direction beside the road.

k1.text: Immediately before turning: mirrors and shoulder check to the right – the cyclist may be in the blind spot.

k2.text: The cyclist is coming from behind and going straight on. Stop and let him through – only then turn right in a tight arc.

frage.text: What do I do now?
optionen: Turn quickly in front of the cyclist
Sound the horn so he brakes
frage.erklaerung: The cyclist has priority. Accidents between right-turning vehicles and cyclists are among the most serious in city traffic.

k3.text: Only turn when it's clear. While turning, keep watching for cyclists and pedestrians – the next cyclist is already coming.

reissverschluss.titel: Zip merge when a lane ends
reissverschluss.kurz: Use both lanes up to the narrowing, then take turns

k0.text: The lane-reduction sign announces: the right-hand lane ends. Both lanes continue to be used up to the narrowing.

frage.text: When do I move to the left?
optionen: Immediately when I see the sign
Immediately before the start of the narrowing
Not at all, the others have to wait
frage.erklaerung: § 7 Abs. 4 StVO: Merge immediately before the start of the narrowing, taking turns.

k1.text: Don't change lanes too early: driving on the right up to the narrowing uses the road correctly and helps keep the queue short.

k2.titel: Indicate and look for a gap
k2.text: Indicate left, match your speed to the left-hand queue and look for the vehicle you will merge behind.

k3.text: Immediately before the narrowing: shoulder check – and merge to the left in turn, after one vehicle. Drivers on the left each let one vehicle in.

frage.text: Who has to let whom in?
optionen: Drivers on the left each let one vehicle in, taking turns
Drivers on the right have to wait until everything is clear
frage.erklaerung: Zip merge (Reißverschlussverfahren): alternately, one from the left, one from the right.

k4.text: The zip merge applies when a lane ends or is blocked. It does NOT apply to the acceleration lane of a motorway slip road – there the through traffic has right of way.

rettungsgasse.kurz: As soon as traffic slows to a crawl: far-left lane moves left, everyone else moves right

k0.text: The traffic is getting slower. As soon as vehicles are only moving at walking pace or everyone has stopped, the emergency corridor (Rettungsgasse) must be formed – not only when the blue lights arrive.

frage.text: When is the emergency corridor formed?
optionen: Only when I hear a siren
As soon as traffic is at walking pace or at a standstill
Only if there are accidents ahead of me
frage.erklaerung: § 11 Abs. 2 StVO: at walking pace or standstill – immediately.

k1.text: The corridor is formed between the far-left lane and the lane immediately to its right: whoever is in the far-left lane moves to the left – everyone else moves to the right.

frage.text: You are in the middle of three lanes. Which way?
frage.erklaerung: All lanes except the far-left one move to the right.

k2.text: Blue lights and siren: clear the way immediately. Stay put, stop manoeuvring back and forth – the corridor must be straight and clear.

k3.text: The corridor stays clear even after an emergency vehicle has passed – often more follow. Don't follow it!

frage.text: The ambulance has passed. What now?
optionen: Keep the corridor open, more may come
Move back into the lane immediately
frage.erklaerung: The emergency corridor remains until traffic is flowing again.

k4.text: The hard shoulder is not a lane for the impatient. Anyone who fails to form the emergency corridor or drives in it themselves risks a fine, penalty points and a driving ban.

rvl.kurz: Who goes first? Three cars at a junction without signs

k0.text: In a 30 km/h zone there are almost never priority signs – here "right before left" (rechts vor links) applies. Approach slowly so that you can stop.

frage.text: Which rule applies at this junction?
optionen: The wider road has right of way
frage.erklaerung: Without signs, traffic lights or police, § 8 Abs. 1 StVO applies: whoever comes from the right has right of way.

k1.text: All three have stopped. Each looks to the right: whoever has nobody there may go first.

frage.text: In which order may the vehicles go?
frage.erklaerung: Blue has nobody on its right and goes first. Then the driving school car (Blue was on its right). Red goes last – the driving school car was on Red's right.

k2.text: The blue car has nobody coming from the right and goes first.

k3.text: Now the right is clear – the driving school car goes straight across the junction.

k4.text: Red turns left. It had to wait because the driving school car came from the right.

k5.text: Whoever has to wait shows this by approaching at moderate speed. If there are cars on all four sides, the drivers communicate – one gives up their right of way.

schulbus.kurz: No overtaking, walking pace – oncoming traffic too – and expect children

k0.text: The school bus is approaching the bus stop with its hazard lights on. It must not be overtaken now.

frage.text: May I overtake the bus while it is approaching the stop with its hazard lights on?
optionen: Yes, if the road is clear
Only if I sound the horn
frage.erklaerung: § 20 Abs. 3 StVO: Public service buses and school buses approaching a stop with their hazard lights on must not be overtaken.

k1.text: It's best to stop behind the bus at a distance first. Children are unpredictable and may run into the road behind or in front of the bus.

k2.text: Only pass at walking pace (about 4–7 km/h) and with enough distance that nobody is endangered. This also applies to oncoming traffic!

frage.text: Does the walking-pace rule also apply to oncoming traffic?
optionen: No, only to the same direction
Yes – oncoming traffic on the same carriageway also drives at walking pace
frage.erklaerung: § 20 Abs. 4 StVO: Walking pace also applies to oncoming traffic on the same carriageway.

k3.text: A child is running across the road in front of the bus. Stop immediately – if necessary, you must wait.

frage.text: What do I do?
optionen: Stop and wait until the child is safely across
frage.erklaerung: If necessary, you must wait – any danger to passengers must be ruled out.

k4.text: The bus indicates left to pull away from the stop. The bus must be allowed to pull away – wait if necessary.

stop.kurz: Always stop completely at the stop line – then edge forward

k0.text: Sign 206 means: stop at the stop line – always, even if the road is clear – and then give way.

frage.text: Do I have to stop at the stop sign even if I can see that the road is clear?
frage.erklaerung: Sign 206: Stopping is mandatory. The wheels must come to a standstill.

k1.text: The car is at the stop line – the wheels are stationary. From here you often can't see enough yet.

k2.text: Edge forward slowly to the sight line and stop again. Look left, right, left.

frage.text: The view is blocked at the stop line. What now?
optionen: Edge forward slowly and look again
frage.erklaerung: After stopping at the stop line you may edge forward carefully to the sight line.

k3.text: Both vehicles on the priority road have right of way. Only turn right when it's clear.

ueberholen.kurz: Check the view, wait for oncoming traffic, overtake briskly, pull back in with distance
ueberholen.worum: Ahead of you is a lorry doing 60 km/h; the limit is 100. Overtaking is one of the most dangerous manoeuvres outside built-up areas: you are driving in the lane of oncoming traffic. It only works if the road is clear far enough ahead.

rf.richtig: You are watching how it's done correctly. The same situation is also available with the mistake that happens most often in practice: following too closely and pulling out without a clear view.
rf.falsch: You are watching the typical mistake. Notice where it goes wrong: the distance, the red area, the headlight flash. Afterwards it's worth comparing it directly with the correct version.

lkw.text: Outside built-up areas, the limit is 100 km/h, and a lorry ahead is doing 60. Keep enough distance, at least half the speedometer reading in metres. That way you can see past it and build up speed.

frage.text: When may I overtake?
optionen: Only if it is clear that oncoming traffic will not be obstructed during the whole overtaking manoeuvre, and I am significantly faster
frage.erklaerung: § 5 Abs. 2 StVO: Only overtake if obstruction of oncoming traffic is ruled out, and at a significantly higher speed.

gegen.text: A car is coming towards you. Don't pull out now – wait. The green or red area shows whether the required roughly 500 m are clear.

frage.text: Roughly how much clear road do I need to overtake a lorry doing 60 km/h at 100 km/h?
optionen: About 250 m overtaking distance, and in that time oncoming traffic covers about the same distance again: around 500 m of visibility
frage.erklaerung: Overtaking distance ≈ (both vehicle lengths + gap before and after) × v₁ ÷ (v₁ − v₂) ≈ 100 m × 100 ÷ 40 ≈ 250 m. In the same time, oncoming traffic covers roughly the same distance again.

sichern.text: The road is clear and you can see well ahead, no solid line. Interior and exterior mirrors, shoulder check to the left, then indicate left. Start building up a little speed already.

vorbei.text: Pull out and accelerate briskly. The speed limit remains the limit. Keep sufficient side clearance from the lorry.

frage.text: The lorry speeds up while being overtaken. Is it allowed to?
optionen: No, a vehicle being overtaken must not increase its speed
frage.erklaerung: § 5 Abs. 6 StVO: A vehicle being overtaken must not increase its speed.

einordnen.text: Interior mirror: only when you can see the whole lorry in it, indicate right and move back in. Don't cut in just in front of it.

verbot.text: First the warning line with short gaps announces the solid line, then Sign 276 applies. Here a farm track joins from the right, and the tractor there wants to get onto the road. An overtaking manoeuvre already started must be completed before this point.

frage.text: May I cross the solid centre line to overtake?
frage.erklaerung: The lane boundary line (Sign 295) must not be crossed.

f_dicht.text: Only 12 m distance at 60 km/h. The lorry blocks your view ahead: you can't see whether oncoming traffic is coming. At least 30 m would be correct.

frage.text: What distance is correct at 60 km/h (rule of thumb)?
frage.erklaerung: Rule of thumb outside built-up areas: half the speedometer reading in metres, i.e. 30 m at 60 km/h. That is about 2 seconds.

f_raus.titel: Pulling out without a clear view
f_raus.text: Pulled out straight after the first oncoming vehicle, without a shoulder check, without building up speed and without knowing what comes next. The area is red: the van is already too close.

frage.text: What would have helped here?
optionen: Dropping back, increasing the distance and only overtaking when the road is definitely clear
frage.erklaerung: Overtaking is not permitted when the traffic situation is unclear (§ 5 Abs. 3 Nr. 1 StVO). With more distance you can see whether the road is clear.

f_gegen.text: The van brakes and flashes its headlights. Anyone who obstructs oncoming traffic should not have overtaken. Now only a dangerous cut-in is left.

f_knapp.text: Straight into the gap, only a few metres in front of the lorry. The lorry has to brake. When overtaking, you must not obstruct the overtaken vehicle when moving back in.

f_besser.titel: This is how it should have been done
f_besser.text: Keep your distance, wait for oncoming traffic and only overtake, with a run-up, when the road is definitely clear. If in doubt: don't overtake. Tip: take a look at the "The right way" version.

merken: Only overtake if you can see the road clearly and oncoming traffic will not be obstructed during the whole overtaking manoeuvre, and only at a significantly higher speed.
Don't overtake when the traffic situation is unclear. If in doubt: stay behind.
Before pulling out: mirrors, shoulder check, indicator. When moving back in, don't obstruct the vehicle you have overtaken.
A vehicle being overtaken must not speed up.
Rule of thumb: to pass a lorry doing 60 km/h at 100 km/h, you need around 250 m of overtaking distance and around 500 m of clear view.

voreinander.titel: Two left-turners: turning in front of each other
voreinander.kurz: Opposing left-turners turn in front of each other

k0.text: The driving school car and the red car both want to turn left and are facing each other.

frage.text: How do the two turn?
optionen: In front of each other – each turns in front of the other
Whoever is there first goes first
frage.erklaerung: § 9 Abs. 4 StVO: Opposing left-turners turn in front of each other – unless the traffic situation or the layout of the junction requires otherwise.

k1.titel: Turning in front of each other
k1.text: Both set off at the same time and turn in front of each other – the cars pass right side to right side. This saves time – but the other left-turner blocks the view of the oncoming traffic behind it, so pay particular attention.

k2.text: Turn around each other (passing behind each other) only if road markings, traffic lights or the layout of the junction require it.

wenden.kurz: Turning around by driving forwards and backwards in a narrow road

k0.text: Stop at the right-hand edge. Check: Is turning allowed here and can you see well? Indicate left and look in both directions.

frage.text: What is the most important check when turning around?
optionen: Watching in both directions before every move
frage.erklaerung: When turning around, nobody may be endangered (§ 9 Abs. 5 StVO) – observation is the key point.

k1.text: Move off slowly while steering fully to the left – until just before the opposite kerb. Just before stopping, already start steering back to the right.

k2.text: Reverse gear, look all around again, reverse slowly and steer fully to the right – until just before the kerb behind you.

frage.text: Which way do I steer when reversing?
optionen: Right – the rear should go to the right
frage.erklaerung: When reversing: turn the steering wheel in the direction you want the rear to go.

k3.titel: 3rd move: forwards, out to the left
k3.text: Observe once more, steer fully to the left and drive off in the new direction. Move to the right.

k4.text: Don't steer while stationary, but while the car is rolling slowly. The number of moves is secondary – the kerb must not be touched.

zebra.kurz: Look ahead, be ready to brake – anyone who wants to cross has priority

k0.text: Ease off the accelerator early and watch the pavements: Does someone want to cross? Children are small and hard to see.

frage.text: How do I approach a zebra crossing when someone clearly wants to cross?
optionen: Carry on as normal, they have to wait
Only at moderate speed, waiting if necessary
Sound the horn and drive through
frage.erklaerung: § 26 Abs. 1 StVO: Allow pedestrians to cross, approach only at moderate speed, wait if necessary.

k1.text: The pedestrians start to cross – stop before the crossing, not on it. Overtaking or passing the waiting car is prohibited.

frage.text: The car in front of me stops at the zebra crossing. May I overtake it on the left?
optionen: No – overtaking is not allowed at pedestrian crossings
frage.erklaerung: § 26 Abs. 3 StVO: Overtaking is not allowed at pedestrian crossings.

k2.text: Only drive on when everyone has safely left the crossing – on the other side too. Eye contact helps.

k3.text: If traffic is backed up beyond the crossing, don't drive onto the zebra crossing if you would have to wait on it.
